candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide community education, identify health risks and warning signs, support early intervention, and connect individuals with appropriate preventive or health-care resources.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — community mental-health literacy and early intervention
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize Mental Health First Aid as an early-intervention community training program focused on recognizing challenges, providing initial support, and connecting people with appropriate help rather than diagnosing or replacing professional treatment.

options.A: Teach community members to recognize mental-health or substance-use challenges, provide initial support, and help connect the person with appropriate professional or community care.
options.B: Teach community members to diagnose psychiatric disorders and independently select definitive treatment plans.
options.C: Train nonclinicians to replace professional services by providing ongoing psychotherapy and medication management.
options.D: Teach participants to avoid responding until a licensed clinician is physically present.

candidate.rationale: Current Mental Health First Aid USA guidance describes MHFA as early-intervention training that teaches people to identify, understand, and respond to signs of mental-health or substance-use challenges, provide an initial level of support, and help connect the person with appropriate professional or other support. MHFA explicitly states that First Aiders do not diagnose mental illness and do not provide therapy or replace professional treatment. Therefore A is correct. B and C assign diagnostic/treatment roles outside the program, while D contradicts the purpose of equipping community members to offer safe initial support before or while professional help is being accessed.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Mental Health First Aid trains community members to recognize and respond to mental-health/substance-use challenges, provide initial support, and connect people with appropriate help; it does not train them to diagnose or replace professional treatment.
